transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess what finally scared me into coming in is... I'm having some trouble at work. I just keep making these really dumb technical mistakes that I know better than to make. 

Like... labeling camera cards wrong, or missing a timecode note. Recently I exported a client cut with the wrong lower-third, even after I swore I checked it. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you struggled with this kind of forgetfulness and lack of attention for most of your life, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

Um... no, it's not new. I guess it's been most of my life. Like... even back in elementary school, the teachers used to have to move my desk. I was just... always out of my seat, or blurting answers out. Bothering the other kids before I even realized I was doing it. So... yeah. Not new.

Looking at your life today, apart from the trouble with focus at work, do you still find that you struggle with feeling physically restless, or do you find yourself frequently interrupting others or acting before thinking?

Um... yeah, I guess so. 

Like... if I have to sit still through a client screening, it's... it feels like there’s this pressure building up under my skin. I just feel like I need to get up and do something with my body... even when I know I’m supposed to just watch quietly. So... yeah. I guess I'm still restless.
In your day-to-day life, do you find that you frequently interrupt others while they are speaking?

Um... yeah, sometimes. I mean... I guess I catch myself cutting in when people are talking. Or... like, at work, I'll just lean over an assistant's shoulder and fix something on their timeline. Even if they didn't ask. I know it probably looks like I don't trust them, but... I just kind of do it before I think. So... yeah.

When you look at your daily life, do you feel that your struggles with focus and attention are just as significant as your struggles with restlessness and impulsivity, or does one of those two areas feel like a much bigger problem for you?
Um... I don't know. I guess... they're both just there. I haven't really thought about which one is worse. It's just... how it is.
